 JUDGMENT
This petition under Section 166 MV Act is filed by the Petitioner seeking compensation of .25,00,000/- for the injuries sustained in a road traffic accident.

2. It is stated that on 30-06-2023 at about 7.30 P.M., the Petitioner was proceeding on his motorcycle bearing No.KA-02-JF-9149 opposite Ambur Dum 2nd Biriyani Hotel, Syndicate Bank Colony, Andarahalli main road, Bengaluru.

At that time, the rider of another motorcycle bearing No.KA-02-KC-4143, (hereinafter called as offending vehicle) rode the said vehicle at a very high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and collided with his two wheeler.

As a result of the impact,
the Petitioner fell down and sustained crushed injuries to his right leg, right hand alongwith other bleeding injuries.
He was immediately taken to Athishaya Hospital, Andrahalli, then he was shifted to Boss hospital, Kamakshipalya, Bengaluru, Where he was admitted as an inpatient and underwent surgery.

due to the severity and irreparable injuries sustained, particularly to the right leg,
amputation of the right leg was medically necessitated and performed.
The petitioner has thereby suffered permanent disability, which has severally impacted his ability to lead a normal life as he did prior to the accident.
3. It is claimed that the Petitioner incurred Rs.2,00,000/- towards medical treatment, conveyance and incidental charges.
At the time of accident, Petitioner was 65 years old, working as plumber and was earning .30,000/- P.M.

Due to accidental 2nd injuries sustained and the resulting disability,
he has suffered a significant loss of earning capacity and income.

Since the accident occurred solely due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending vehicle, the petitioner prays that suitable compensation be awarded against Respondent No.1- Insurer and Respondent No.2-Insured.
4. In response to the petition notice, the Respondent No.2 has appeared through counsel, and filed the written statement.
The respondent No.1 remained absent and was placed exparte.
5. In the written statement, the respondent no 2 admitted issuing of a liability only insurance policy but stated that their liability is subject to terms and conditions of the said policy.
They have further contended that the owner of the offending vehicle and the concerned police have not complied the mandatory provisions of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act.

Respondent no 2 denied the negligence of the driver of offending vehicle and further contended that the driver of the offending vehicle was not holding valid DL and he was a minor at time of the accident and concerned 2nd police have filed Krishnappa vs Pradeep J on 7 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/146819515/
2 charge sheet U/s.3(1), 181 of MV Act and as such, this respondent is not liable to pay any compensation.

It is also denied the nature of injuries, the occupation and income of the Petitioner,
the disability and the amount claimed as compensation, terming it as excessive and exaggerated.
On these grounds, they have prayed for dismissal of the petition.

6. On the basis of the above pleadings, the following Issues were framed :-
1.

Whether the Petitioner proves that on 30-06-2023 at about 7-30 p.m., on Andrahalli to Magadi main road opposite of Ambur Dum Biriyani hotel, Syndicate Bank layout, he sustained injuries in a road traffic accident, while he was moving on his motorcycle bearing number KA-02- JF-9149 due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the motorcycle bearing number KA-02-KC-4143?
2. Whether the respondent No.2 proves that there is violation of the policy conditions by respondent No.1 and respondent No.2 is not liable to pay any compensation?
2nd 3.

if any, how much, from whom?

The petitioner has thereby suffered permanent disability, which has severally impacted his ability to lead a normal life as he did prior to the accident.
12. PW1, deposed that the accident was solely due to rash and negligent act of the rider of the 2nd offending vehicle.

PW1 has produced copy of FIR at Ex.P.1, statement at Ex.P.2, rough sketch at Ex.P.3, spot mahazar at Ex.P.4, notice, reply at Ex.P.5 & 6, IMV report at Ex.P.7, Wound certificate at Ex.P8, charge sheet at Ex.P.9 and order sheet in CC.11540/2023 at Ex.P.10.

13. As per wound certificate he has sustained following injuries:
1. Laceration present over front distal third of right leg.
2. Crush injury present over right ankle joint and extending to dorsum of right foot.
Doctor opined that both injuries are grievous in nature.
14. It is pertinent to note that Respondent No. 2- Insurance Company has not placed any cogent material on record to disprove the negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.

In the absence of substantive rebuttal evidence, either oral or documentary, from the respondents, the presumption 2nd of negligence on the part of the rider of the offending vehicle remains unshaken.
15. The evidence adduced by PW-1, including the First Information Report (FIR), charge sheet, and medical records, corroborates the petitioner's version of the accident.

There is nothing elicited in the cross- examination of PW-1 to discredit his testimony, and no material has been brought forth by the respondent no 2 to counter or contradict the documentary evidence produced by the petitioner.
16. It is a well-settled principle of law that proceedings under the Motor Vehicles Act are beneficial in nature, and the standard of proof of negligence is not akin to that of a criminal trial.
The Tribunal is not required to insist on strict proof of rash and negligent driving where the surrounding circumstances and police records collectively support the petitioner's case.
17. The charge sheet filed by the investigating police officer against the driver of the offending vehicle prima facie establishes rash and negligent riding on the part of the said rider.
The accident and resulting , 2nd grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner are clearly attributable to the negligent act of the rider of the offending vehicle.
Accordingly, this Tribunal holds that the accident occurred solely due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending vehicle.

26. ISSUE NO.3 :-The petitioner has stated that due to the accident dated 13-06-2023, he sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident, he was taken to Asthishaya Hospital, Andrahalli,
and subsequently shifted to Boss Hospital, Kamakshi Palya, Bengaluru, where he underwent treatment as an inpatient and multiple surgeries, culminating in the amputation of his right leg below the knee.
27. The petitioner has further deposed that at the time of the accident, he was working as a plumber and earning more than 30,000 per month.
Due to the injuries sustained and the resultant amputation, he is unable to continue his work as before and has suffered a substantial loss of income.
He also contends that he has lost his normal life and is facing difficulty in carrying out day-to-day activities.

28. In support of his case, PW2, Medical Records Department (MRD) official of Boss Multi-Specialty Hospital, has produced relevant medical documents, , 2nd including the MLC Register, case sheet, and X-ray films, marked as Exhibits P18 to P20.
29.

Further, PW3, Dr. S.A. Somashekara, Orthopedic Surgeon at Boring and Lady Curzon Hospital,
Bengaluru, deposed that the petitioner had sustained a crush injury to the right foot and ankle with doubtful viability, and ultimately underwent a below-knee amputation of the right leg on 01-07-2023.

30. PW3 has assessed the disability of the particular limb at 60% and the whole-body disability at 40%.
However, during the course of cross- examination, he stated that he did not treat the petitioner personally and he had seen the wound certificate or the discharge summary.
The amputation was done approximately 20 cm below the knee.
He did not measure the contra lateral (other) limb during the disability assessment.
He admitted that he assessed only physical disability, and not functional , 2nd disability.
He denied that the 60% limb disability was assessed contrary to standard disability guidelines.
31. The petitioner sustained a crush injury to the right hand and amputation of the right lower limb below the knee, resulting in a severe and permanent disability.

This condition has a direct and substantial impact on the petitioner's earning capacity, particularly considering his profession as a plumber, which requires physical mobility, manual dexterity, and the ability to maintain body Krishnappa vs Pradeep J on 7 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/146819515/

sentences.text: It is a well-established fact that the lower limb plays a critical role in mobility, balance, and the performance of routine daily tasks.

Any impairment to the leg not only affects the petitioner's personal and social life, but also significantly hampers his ability to carry out vocational duties,
especially in a physically demanding trade like plumbing.

33. While PW3, the doctor, assessed the physical disability at 40% to the whole body, it is pertinent to note that no specific opinion was given regarding functional disability, which refers to the actual impact of the physical impairment on the earning potential of , 2nd the petitioner.

Taking into consideration the nature and location of the injury, the degree of disability sustained, its functional impact on daily and vocational activities, the age and avocation of the petitioner, this Tribunal is of the considered opinion that the functional disability should be reasonably assessed at 25% to the whole body, rather than 40% as assessed purely on physical grounds.
This assessment shall be taken into account for the purpose of computing compensation for future loss of earning capacity.

Thus this tribunal is of the opinion that the petitioner who sustained the injuries is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
34. Loss of future income on account of permanent disability:
It is not in dispute that the petitioner suffered amputation of the right leg due to the injuries sustained in the road traffic accident.
On perusal of the medical records and the deposition of PW3, it is evident that the petitioner underwent surgery, resulting in below-knee amputation of the right leg.
Due to the said amputation, the petitioner is unable to , 2nd carry out his avocation as earlier.
Hence, this Tribunal holds that the petitioner has suffered a functional disability to the extent of 25%.
35. The petitioner has stated that he was 65 years of age at the time of the accident.
In support of his age, he has produced Exhibit P-13 driving licence which records his date of birth as 02-09-1961.
The same is corroborated by various medical records which reflect his age as 62 years.
Therefore, for the purpose of assessing compensation, the petitioner's age is considered as 62 years on the date of the accident.
36. The appropriate multiplier applicable is 7, as laid down by Hon'ble Apex court in Sarla Verma's case is at 7.
Then, loss of future income comes to considering the age group of 61-65 years.
37. The petitioner claims to have been working as a plumber, earning a sum of Rs. 30,000 per month.
However, he has not produced any supporting documentary evidence to substantiate his income.

In the absence of such material, this Tribunal is inclined to fix a notional income of Rs.
16,000 per month, which is reasonable.

Then, loss of future income comes to Rs.16,000 x 12 x 7 x 25/100= .3,36,000/-.
39. Pain and sufferings:
So far as non-pecuniary compensation is concerned, it is undisputed that the petitioner has suffered below-knee amputation of the right leg and has undergone multiple hospitalizations and surgeries.
These injuries have undeniably caused immense pain, suffering, and emotional trauma.
The physical agony and mental anguish resulting from such a grievous injury cannot be quantified in exact terms, yet must be duly compensated under settled legal principles.
Therefore, this Tribunal is of the opinion that a sum of 3,00,000 (Rupees Three Lakhs only) would be just and reasonable under the head of pain and suffering.
40. Loss of amenities of life:

Due to the nature of the injury, the petitioner is permanently disabled and will face hardship in performing routine and day- to-day activities, leading to a loss of amenities of life, which includes loss of comfort, frustration, , 2nd disappointment, inconvenience, and reduced quality of life.
Hence, a sum of 1,00,000 is awarded under the head of loss of amenities of life.
41. Medical expenses:
The petitioner has produced medical bills totaling 91,058/- marked as Ex- P-15, in support of the claim for expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, and medicines.
Though Learned Counsel for Respondent No. 2 has cross- examined PW-1, nothing has been elicited in the cross- examination to discredit or challenge the authenticity of the said medical bills.
Upon perusal, the bills appear to be genuine and consistent with the injuries suffered and the treatment undertaken.
Accordingly, this Tribunal awards a sum of 91,058/- under the head of medical expenses.
42. Cost of Artificial Limb (Prosthesis):
The PW-3 doctor has opined that the petitioner requires a sophisticated prosthesis, which is very expensive and essential for basic mobility and daily functioning.
In support of this, the petitioner has examined PW-4,Senior Prosthetist and orthotist and Director of John's Prosthetic and Orthotic center, Austin town, , 2nd Bengaluru.

PW-4 deposed that the petitioner's muscle strength and stump condition were examined, and a prosthesis was recommended that would support K2 and partial K3 level activities, thereby enabling the petitioner to perform routine daily tasks.
43. The cost of the recommended prosthesis is 4,69,000/-, with an expected life span of 8-10 years and a 2-year warranty.
Additionally, maintenance costs are estimated at 40,000/- per annum, and socket replacement may be required based on stump variation.

44. Considering the petitioner's age of 62 years, the necessity and benefit of the prosthesis in improving mobility and quality of life, and balancing the cost factor, this Tribunal deems it just and appropriate to award a sum of 3,00,000/- towards the cost of the artificial limb (prosthesis).
45. Conveyance, food, nourishment and attendant charges:
As per Exhibit P-11 (Discharge Card), the petitioner was treated as an inpatient at Boss Multi-Specialty Hospital, Bengaluru from 03.06.2023 to 07.06.2023, i.e., for a total duration of 5 , 2nd days.

Taking into account the cost of transportation Krishnappa vs Pradeep J on 7 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/146819515/
8 to and from the hospital, expenses towards food and nourishment during hospitalization, and attendant/care giver charges, this Tribunal finds it just and reasonable to award a sum of 10,000/-
under this head.
46. Disfigurement:
The petitioner has produced Ex P-16 and Ex P-17, which are photographs clearly showing the amputation of the right leg below the knee.
The condition of the petitioner, as seen from these photographs, is serious and indicative of severe permanent disfigurement.
The amputation has not only caused physical disfigurement but also severely affected the petitioner's self-esteem, mobility, and dependency on others for day-to-day activities.
Considering the gravity and visible disfigurement, a sum of 50,000/- is awarded under the head of disfigurement.
47. Loss of earning during laid up period:
The accident occurred on 30.06.2023, and the petitioner has claimed loss of income during the period of treatment and recovery.

Given the nature of injuries,
, 2nd multiple hospitalizations, and amputation, a conservative laid down period of 3 months is considered appropriate.
The petitioner's notional monthly income has already been taken as 16,000/- per month.

Therefore, the loss of income during the laid down period is computed as:16,000  3 months = 48,000/-Hence, a sum of 48,000/- is awarded under the head of loss of income during the period of treatment.

. Liability:

As already discussed under Issue No. 2, it has been clearly established that Respondent No.1 has violated the terms and conditions of the insurance policy, particularly in view of the fact that the driver of the offending vehicle was not holding a valid and effective driving license as on the date of the accident.
Therefore, Respondent No.2 (Insurance Company) is not liable to indemnify the insured for the claim made under the present petition.
Consequently, Respondent No. 1, being the owner of the offending vehicle, is held liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

sentences.text: The learned counsel for the petitioner has argued that, notwithstanding the violation of policy terms, the Tribunal ought to have directed the insurance company to pay the compensation initially and thereafter recover the same from the insured, invoking the principle of "pay and recovery".

In support of this contention, reliance was placed on certain decisions rendered between First Appeal from order No.1780/2024 - ICICI Lombard Gen.Ins.Co.Ltd., Vs. Smt.Arti Devi and others and (2018) 9 SCC 650 - , 2nd Shamanna and another Vs. Divisional Manager, Oriental Ins.Co.Ltd., and others.

sentences.text: 51. However, upon careful perusal material on record and legal position, it is pertinent to note that the Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Act, 2019, particularly relevant provisions that impact liability of insurers, came into effect from 15-02-2022.
Since this amendment relates to substantive rights, it has only prospective effect, and cannot be applied retrospectively to the present case.

52. Furthermore, the petitioner relied upon a recent decision of the ICICI Lombard Gen.Ins.Co.Ltd.,
Vs. Smt.Arti Devi and others, in support of the "pay and recover" doctrine.
However, it is noted that the Hon'ble Apex Court has stayed the operation of the said judgment.
Therefore, the principle laid down therein cannot be treated as binding precedent, and this Tribunal does not find it appropriate to rely upon that judgment in the present context.

Hence, in the facts and circumstances of the case,
the principle of pay and recover does not arise, and the liability to pay compensation rests solely with Respondent , 2nd No.1, the owner of the offending vehicle.
I answer Issue No.3 partly in the affirmative.
53. ISSUE NO.4 :

In view of the above discussion, reasons stated and findings given to Issue Nos. 1 to 3, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER Claim Petition filed under Sec.166 of M.V.Act is allowed in part with cost.

Petitioner is awarded compensation of .12,35,058/- together with interest @ 6% p.a.
(except future medical expenses) from the date of petition till the date of deposit with the Tribunal.
Respondent No.1 - RC owner shall pay the aforesaid amount within two months from the date of this order.

Out of the total compensation amount, 25% shall be kept in FD in the name of Petitioner in any nationalized bank of his choice for a period of 3 years and remaining 75% amount along with interest shall be released in favour of the Petitioner through E-payment on proper identification and verification.
Advocate's fee is fixed at .1,000/-.
, 2nd Draw award accordingly.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
In the absence of substantive rebuttal evidence, either oral or documentary, from the respondents, the presumption 2nd of negligence on the part of the rider of the offending vehicle remains unshaken.
15. The evidence adduced by PW-1, including the First Information Report (FIR), charge sheet, and medical records, corroborates the petitioner's version of the accident.
There is nothing elicited in the cross- examination of PW-1 to discredit his testimony, and no material has been brought forth by the respondent no 2 to counter or contradict the documentary evidence produced by the petitioner.
16. It is a well-settled principle of law that proceedings under the Motor Vehicles Act are beneficial in nature, and the standard of proof of negligence is not akin to that of a criminal trial.
The Tribunal is not required to insist on strict proof of rash and negligent driving where the surrounding circumstances and police records collectively support the petitioner's case.
17. The charge sheet filed by the investigating police officer against the driver of the offending vehicle prima facie establishes rash and negligent riding on the part of the said rider.
The accident and resulting , 2nd grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner are clearly attributable to the negligent act of the rider of the offending vehicle.
Accordingly, this Tribunal holds that the accident occurred solely due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending vehicle.
Respondent No. 2-Insurance Company has specifically contended that the owner of the offending vehicle violated the terms and conditions of the insurance policy, inasmuch as the driver was not holding a valid and effective Driving License (DL) as on the date of the accident.
It is a well-established fact that the lower limb plays a critical role in mobility, balance, and the performance of routine daily tasks.
Any impairment to the leg not only affects the petitioner's personal and social life, but also significantly hampers his ability to carry out vocational duties,
especially in a physically demanding trade like plumbing.
Taking into consideration the nature and location of the injury, the degree of disability sustained, its functional impact on daily and vocational activities, the age and avocation of the petitioner, this Tribunal is of the considered opinion that the functional disability should be reasonably assessed at 25% to the whole body, rather than 40% as assessed purely on physical grounds.
This assessment shall be taken into account for the purpose of computing compensation for future loss of earning capacity.
Thus this tribunal is of the opinion that the petitioner who sustained the injuries is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
34. Loss of future income on account of permanent disability:
On perusal of the medical records and the deposition of PW3, it is evident that the petitioner underwent surgery, resulting in below-knee amputation of the right leg.
Due to the said amputation, the petitioner is unable to , 2nd carry out his avocation as earlier.
Therefore, for the purpose of assessing compensation, the petitioner's age is considered as 62 years on the date of the accident.
The physical agony and mental anguish resulting from such a grievous injury cannot be quantified in exact terms, yet must be duly compensated under settled legal principles.
